title: Parse a CLI Contract
concept: Preserve arguments and reject ambiguous input

writing.summary: Preserve arguments and reject ambiguous input.
writing.rule: Parse the entire invocation before applying any side effect.
writing.explanation:
A shell groups text into arguments before a Rust program sees it. Quotes preserve a space or an empty argument; they are not usually part of the resulting argument. Cargo consumes its options before the double dash and passes the remainder to the executable. The first executable argument is conventionally the program name and is not a user command.

Task Ledger accepts exactly `list` or `add TITLE`. Reject an unknown command, a missing title and extra arguments. Trim the title for domain validation, while retaining internal spaces and Unicode. Do not partially add a task before discovering a later invalid option. The independent lab takes only the already-separated user arguments; the companion main passes `std::env::args().skip(1)`.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Run cargo run -- add "learn Rust" and cargo run -- add "" against the companion CLI.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.
writing.exampleCaption: The worked implementation exercises preserve arguments and reject ambiguous input. Its tests demonstrate the stated finite contract.
writing.task: Accept exactly list or add plus one nonblank title. Return list or add:TITLE with the title trimmed; reject every other shape with Err("usage"). Keep the public signature. Open the compiler lab and edit solution.rs; do not edit the private verification caller.
writing.success: The separate caller accepts the changed solution and rejects unchanged TODO, a wrong implementation and a printed success message.
writing.question: Which invocation passes one title containing a space?
answers: Quotes always become part of the Rust title
writing.feedback: The shell supplies argument boundaries; Cargo needs the double dash before application arguments.
